facts.value: sTec, Inc. (Santa Ana, California; enterprise solid state drives; Nasdaq: STEC)
Western Digital Corporation (WDC), through its wholly-owned subsidiary Lodi Ventures, Inc. (merger sub)
Strategic (storage-products developer and manufacturer; WD, HGST and G-Technology brands)
$6.85 per share in cash, without interest; no financing condition; options and RSUs assumed and converted into WDC awards; $9.4 million target termination fee
DEFM14A (definitive proxy statement) dated 08/07/2013; EDGAR filing date 08/08/2013 per supplied file

target-led: the board decided on a market check in mid-November 2012 and ran the 04/01/2013 outreach; activist Balch Hill/Potomac pressed for strategic alternatives from 12/06/2012; Company A (11/2012), B, C, D and H approached on their own

Undated informal approaches from third parties over the years, 'general and exploratory' with no terms proposed; a 2011 lunch where WDC's then CEO John Coyne said WDC wanted to expand in SSDs; a summer 2012 lunch where WDC's Michael Hajeck asked about the Moshayedis' retirement plans. No further WDC discussion until the process (pp. 23–24).
Met (process 1): 6 parties (Company E, Company D, Company F, Company G, Company H, and WDC through an addendum to its 01/29/2009 NDA)
Yes (asset-only interest from Company C, Company E, Company F and six strategics overall produced no proposals)

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices
facts.value: US dollars per share; all bids per share
BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated), approved 03/26/2013, engagement letter 03/28/2013
Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP (outside corporate counsel); Latham & Watkins LLP (litigation counsel to sTec and Manouch Moshayedi)

As losses mounted and activist Balch Hill pressed for change, sTec's board decided in late 2012 to test a sale, set up a special committee on 02/13/2013 and hired BofA Merrill Lynch in late March. From 04/01/2013 BofA contacted 18 prospective acquirers; six signed NDAs, most interested parties wanted only select assets, and WDC, Company D and Company H gave non-binding indications of $6.60–$7.10, $5.75 and $5.00–$5.75. WDC and Company D were invited to a final round; WDC bid $9.15 with a merger agreement markup and confirmed it as best and final, while Company D kept asking for more time. The board chose WDC on 05/30, but WDC withdrew the next day, and Company D disengaged on 06/05. WDC came back at $6.60–$7.10, was told to name one best price, offered $6.85 on 06/14, and signed on 06/23/2013; the deal was announced on 06/24.

E5 tests: (a) met, since nothing was pending with A; (b) not established, as the gap is under three months and no end was reported (the board 'made a determination to continue', p. 24); (c) met by the 02/13 committee.
